WA Rapper Kayps Channels Family History and Noonkanbah Protest Legacy in Debut Album 'Bunuba Baby'

Western Australian rapper Kurrungaya Bieundurry, known professionally as Kayps, has drawn on his family's deep connection to Indigenous land rights for his acclaimed debut album, *Bunuba Baby*. Released in August, the record reached number two on the Australian hip-hop charts and has received major award nominations, including recognition at the J Awards.

Family Legacy and the Noonkanbah Protest

Inspiration for the album's cover came when Kayps discovered a historical photograph of his grandfather participating in the 1979 Noonkanbah protest. During the historic event, family members and community leaders locked arms at a sacred site in the Kimberley region to blockade drilling trucks from an oil company.

  • Cover Art: Features three generations of his family, including a traditional *Pirlirr* symbol painted by his father.
  • Protest History: Although the blockade was eventually broken by police, the demonstration became a landmark moment for the Kimberley land rights movement.

Musical Upbringing and Evolution

Growing up in the remote Kimberley town of Wangkatjungka before moving to Perth, Kayps was surrounded by a musical family that included a blues artist grandmother and a guitarist-singer father. He began busking with the didgeridoo at age 13 to purchase music production software.

Reflecting on his artistic growth, Kayps acknowledged that his earlier music featured abrasive and immature themes. In contrast, *Bunuba Baby* reflects a more politically conscious voice shaped by late-night discussions with his father and uncle about systemic issues, culture, and community responsibilities.

Addressing Systemic Issues

The album also features intentional commentary regarding law enforcement and systemic pressures faced by First Nations communities. Beyond his music, Kayps aims to connect with younger generations through community workshops, encouraging others to explore and embrace their cultural heritage.

Practical Implications and Verification

Listeners interested in exploring the artist's work or verifying the award nominations and tour details can consult official Australian music charts, public broadcaster announcements from triple j, or Kayps' verified social media and music streaming profiles.
